This vignette introduces the primary settings and configuration APIs, then one
bounded advanced ALA workflow. The repository's deterministic `jc_ci` route is
fixture-backed; the settings example below is deliberately real-data only.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE)
```

## Run a real-data project

Before running `settings.example.yaml`, `site.csv` must exist in the configured
input directory with `site`, `lat`, and `lon` columns. `obs.csv` and `op.csv` are
optional. These input files are not included in the checkout.

After `make bootstrap`, use the source-loading checkout wrapper:

```sh
Rscript scripts/run_project.R settings.example.yaml
```

If `localmap` has been installed as an R package, call the public API directly:

```{r run-settings, eval=FALSE}
localmap::run_settings("settings.example.yaml")
```

Use `cfg_read()` when you need to inspect a complete named profile without
starting the pipeline:

```{r read-config}
cfg <- localmap::cfg_read(profile = "jc_ci")
names(cfg$data)
```

## Bounded advanced ALA example

The advanced ALA functions support a controlled workflow below settings. This
example limits resolution and acquisition to the first requested taxon and is
not evaluated during the vignette build because it requires live ALA access.

```{r ala-example, eval=FALSE}
requests <- localmap::read_species_requests("metadata/species_requests.csv")
one_taxon <- localmap::ala_resolve_species(requests[1, , drop = FALSE])
occurrences <- localmap::ala_fetch_occurrences(
  one_taxon,
  min_year = 2020,
  state_province = "Tasmania"
)
head(occurrences)
```

## Experimental exports

`ala_configure()`, `fetch_layer_registry()`, and `generate_topo_tile_map()` are
experimental lower-level controls. New end-to-end work should begin with
`run_settings()`; use `cfg_read()` and the grouped stable reference when
lower-level control is required.
